newsitem.title: CANADA: TCPL sees lower 1997 gas tranport tolls.
newsitem.headline: TCPL sees lower 1997 gas tranport tolls.

text.p: TransCanada PipeLines Ltd said on Thursday it expected to charge lower tolls for transporting natural gas on its Canadian mainline in 1997, partly because of a recently implemented incentive settlement with its shippers.

"It's too soon to know exactly what our tolls will be in 1997, but on the basis of what we've seen so far, we expect the eastern zone toll could decline to the 85 cents (Canadian) per gigajoule range, compared to the 1996 toll of 90.7 cents per gigajoule," TransCanada senior vice-president Bob Reid said in a statement.

The four-year incentive agreement is aimed at aligning the interests of TransCanada and its shippers and allowing them to share the benefits of reduced costs and higher revenue from discretionary service.
Under the deal's terms, shippers' share of discretionary revenue earned in 1996 -- about C$31.6 million -- will be credited to the overall cost of service for the pipeline in 1997.
Tolls are also reduced when deliveries increase, TransCanada said.
Deliveries in 1997 are forecast to be 2.46 trillion cubic feet, up from 2.43 TCF in 1996, as a result of expansions in 1996 and those planned for 1997.

Also included in the forecast is a potential reduction in TransCanada's 1997 rate of return on common equity due to declining interest rates for long-term Canadian bonds, which are used by Canada's National Energy Board to calculate the company's regulated return, it said.
